destination.name: Kanangra-Boyd National Park
destination.tagline: A wilderness park of sandstone cliffs and gorges, with Jenolan Caves on its doorstep.
destination.description: Kanangra-Boyd National Park is part of the Greater Blue Mountains Area World Heritage Property, about 180 km from Sydney. Its best-known sight is Kanangra Walls, sheer sandstone cliffs with a waterfall and a 10-minute, wheelchair-accessible walk from the car park. The park runs to 686 sq km of gorges and wild rivers, with echidnas and lyrebirds most often seen in summer. It adjoins Jenolan Caves, and the single dirt access road is passable in a 2WD car.
whyVisit: Look over Kanangra Walls' sandstone cliffs
Visit Jenolan Caves once it reopens
Camp among snow gums at Boyd River

goodToKnow.title: Jenolan Caves is closed
goodToKnow.detail: The Jenolan Caves precinct is closed for Two Mile road repairs, with reopening planned for early 2027 (not confirmed), so check the caves site before you plan around it.

goodToKnow.title: Dirt road, no transport
goodToKnow.detail: The only road in is unpaved and bumpy but fine for 2WD, there is no public transport, and the park can close for poor weather or fire danger.

goodToKnow.title: Bring food and the fee
goodToKnow.detail: There is nowhere to eat in the park, and Wikivoyage lists a fee of about $7 per vehicle per day, so bring food and check the NPWS page for the current fee.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Visit in {months}: NSW National Parks says echidnas and lyrebirds are easiest to spot in summer, and canyoning is popular in the warmer months.
